summary: Barbara A. Holdrege is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. She served at the University of California, Santa Barbara, as Associate Professor of the Comparative History of Religions (attested 2000) and later as Professor (attested 2026).

Barbara E. Ward (1919–1983) studied at Newnham College, the LSE, and the University of London. Working in Sinology, she taught history at London (~1948–1955), lectured at Cambridge (~1973–1983), and was a visiting professor at CUHK (1978–1982).

Barbara Gerke, a specialist in Tibetology and religious studies, completed her D.Phil. at Oxford under Charles Ramble and Geoffrey Samuel. She held posts at Humboldt University (2011–2015), Oxford (attested 2017), and the University of Vienna (attested 2026).

Barbara Mittler is a scholar in Sinology, history, and archaeology. She studied at Pearson College London, the Mandarin Training Center, the University of Oxford, and Heidelberg University, where she also held a post in 1993.

Barbara Nimri Aziz is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She earned a B.A. from Queen's University at Kingston and a Ph.D. at SOAS under Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf, later holding a post at the University of Oran in 2007.

Barbara Stoler Miller (1940–1993) was an Indologist educated at Barnard College, Columbia University, and the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown and Stella Kramrisch. She served as a professor at Barnard College and Columbia University (~1968–1993).

Barbra R. Clayton works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She earned her PhD from McGill University, where she was supervised by Richard P. Hayes and Katherine K. Young, and later held a post at Mount Allison University (attested 2013).

Barend Faddegon (1874–1955) was a scholar in Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of Amsterdam. He served on the faculty at the University of Amsterdam from 1907 to 1944, where he became Emeritus Professor.

Barend J. ter Haar is a Sinologist who earned his PhD at Leiden University under Erik Zürcher. He held positions at Heidelberg University (~1994–2000), Leiden University as Professor (~2000–2013), and the University of Hamburg as Professor (~2018).

Barend Jan Terwiel studied at Utrecht University and the Australian National University (Ph.D.). He held academic posts at ANU, the University of Munich, Leiden University, and Hamburg, where he was Chair of Languages and Cultures of Thailand and Laos (1992–2007).

Barnabás Csongor (1923–2018) was a scholar of Sinology and linguistics. He studied at the Budapest University of Technology and Economics and Eötvös Loránd University, later holding academic posts at Eötvös Loránd University and Princeton University.

Barry Kerzin studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Southern California (MD). Working in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, he held posts at the University of Washington (1985–1989) and the University of Hong Kong (2014–2015, 2021–2022).
Bart Dessein is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy who studied under Charles Willemen. He has served as an Associate Professor at Ghent University (attested 2014–2026).

Bart Gruzalski is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Maryland, College Park, in 1974. He later served as a professor of philosophy at Northeastern University.
Barthold Georg Niebuhr (1776–1831) was a historian who studied at Kiel University. He held academic chairs at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1810–1813) and the University of Bonn (~1823–1831).

Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve (1831–1924) studied at Princeton, Bonn, and Göttingen (Dr. phil.). A scholar of linguistics, he served as Professor of Greek at the University of Virginia (1856–1876) and Professor at Johns Hopkins University (1876–1915).

Bazar Baradiin (1878–1937) was a scholar in Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University in 1902 and was appointed head of the Buryat Scientific Committee in 1922.

Beata Grant is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her Ph.D. from Stanford University (~1981–1987) and served as Associate Professor of Chinese Language and Literature at Washington University in St. Louis (~1989–2018).

Beatrice Erskine Lane (1878–1939) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under William James and Josiah Royce at Radcliffe College and earned an M.A. from Columbia University, later becoming a professor at Otani University in 1921.

Beatrix Pfleiderer (1941–2011) was an Indology scholar who studied at Heidelberg University. She taught at the University of Maryland (1971–1975) and held posts at Heidelberg, the University of Hamburg (1982), and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1989–1991).
